Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller piece of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a **base case** — a simple condition that returns a value without calling itself again — otherwise it would loop forever. The function keeps breaking the problem down until it hits that base case, and then the answers combine as each call returns back up the chain. A classic example is factorial: `factorial(n)` returns `n * factorial(n-1)`, stopping when `n` reaches `1`.
